chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail and Ibn Mahbub, altogether from Hanan ibn Sadeer, from his father who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'Which act of worship is the most superior?' So he said: 'There is nothing more superior in the sight of God, Mighty and Majestic, than that He should be asked and sought from for what is with Him. And there is no one more hateful to God, Mighty and Majestic, than one who is too arrogant to worship Him and does not ask for what is with Him.'

key_terms.أَفْضَل: Most superior/best — used in the comparative and superlative forms to indicate what God holds most dear
key_terms.الْعِبَادَة: Worship — any act of devotion and submission to God, ranging from ritual acts (prayer, fasting) to ethical conduct and supplications
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Mighty and Majestic — an honorific epithet for God frequently used in Shia hadith literature, emphasizing His absolute power and glory
key_terms.يَسْتَكْبِر: Arrogance/to be too proud — refusing to ask God out of pride is presented as the gravest spiritual failing
key_terms.يُسْأَل: To be asked/supplicated — God is the recipient of supplication, and this hadith affirms it is the greatest act of worship

ai.seo_question: What is the most superior act of worship according to Imam al-Baqir in Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith records a direct exchange between Sadeer ibn Hakim and Imam al-Baqir (AS), the fifth Imam of the Shia. When asked which act of worship is most superior, the Imam declares that supplication — asking God and seeking from His bounty — surpasses all other acts of worship. The Imam then delivers the complementary warning: arrogance that prevents a person from turning to God in supplication makes one the most detested in God's sight, emphasizing that humility before God is at the heart of true worship.
